name: GPTQ: Accurate Post-Training Quantization for Generative Pre-trained Transformers
problem: Post-training quantization of 100B+ parameter generative models: existing one-shot quantizers lose too much accuracy at 3-4 bits and cannot finish on a feasible compute budget.
mechanism: Layer-by-layer weight quantization that rounds each weight to a grid using approximate second-order (OBS) information: for each linear layer compute the inverse Hessian of the layer inputs H = 2XX^T from calibration activations, Cholesky-factorize it, then walk columns in Cholesky order and greedily pick the rounding of each weight that minimises the layer-output error proxy sum_h (w_h - q_h)^2 / [H^-1]_hh, updating the remaining weights after each choice (the error-compensation step). Sequential-column blocking makes it O(n^3) but GPU-parallel across rows.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract, no hardware named): 175B-parameter GPT models quantized to 3 or 4 bits per weight in ~4 GPU-hours, 'more than doubles the compression gains relative to previously-proposed one-shot quantization methods'; first time a 175B model runs generative inference inside a single GPU. QUALITY COST: described only as 'negligible accuracy degradation relative to the uncompressed baseline' in the abstract - the compression ratio is the load-bearing number, not a paired perplexity delta.
